rules.title: Prohibition on purchasing covered rent coordination services
rules.requirement: A covered real estate lessor, its agent, or its subcontractor must not subscribe to, contract with, or exchange anything of value for the services of a covered service provider.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies in Jersey City to a real estate lessor, its agent, or its subcontractor. A real estate lessor is an individual, corporation, partnership, association, joint-stock company, trust, or unincorporated organization that owns real property and leases all or part of it as a residential dwelling unit. Such a unit must be intended as a person's primary residence and excludes inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities. The purchased services must be those of a service provider: a person performing a coordination function, as defined by the source's reference to Section 1(a)(i)(1), for a real estate lessor or rentor. Person includes a natural person, corporation, partnership, limited liability company, firm, or association. The coordination definition describes collecting nonpublic competitor information from real estate lessors and collecting historical or contemporaneous prices, price changes, supply levels, occupancy rates, or lease or rental contract termination and renewal dates of residential dwelling units from two or more real estate lessors or public databases; computationally analyzing or processing that information; and using that information to recommend rental prices, lease terms, or occupancy levels to a real estate lessor. Nonpublic competitor information is material lease information less than 365 days old that is not widely and readily available to the public at no cost. The coordination definition exempts owners of multiple properties for actions related exclusively to properties controlled by the same rental property owner. Licensed Real Estate Agents operating in accordance with all applicable state regulations are excluded from both the coordination and service-provider definitions.
rules.exemptions: The coordination definition exempts same-owner actions related exclusively to that owner's multiple properties. Compliant Licensed Real Estate Agents are excluded from the coordination and service-provider definitions. The residential dwelling unit definition excludes inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities.
rules.quoted_span:
a.It is unlawful for any real estate lessor, agent, or subcontractor thereof, to subscribe to, contract with, or otherwise
exchange anything of value in return for the services of a Service Provider.

rules.title: Prohibition on facilitating rental noncompetition agreements
rules.requirement: A covered service provider must not facilitate an agreement not to compete among real estate lessors concerning any aspect of residential dwelling units, including rental pricing, fees, or other rental terms.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies in Jersey City to a service provider facilitating an agreement not to compete among real estate lessors concerning residential dwelling units. A service provider is a person performing a coordination function, as defined by the source's reference to Section 1(a)(i)(1), for a real estate lessor or rentor. Person includes a natural person, corporation, partnership, limited liability company, firm, or association. A real estate lessor is an individual, corporation, partnership, association, joint-stock company, trust, or unincorporated organization that owns real property and leases all or part of it as a residential dwelling unit. Such a unit must be intended as a person's primary residence and excludes inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities. The coordination definition describes collecting nonpublic competitor information from real estate lessors and collecting historical or contemporaneous prices, price changes, supply levels, occupancy rates, or lease or rental contract termination and renewal dates of residential dwelling units from two or more real estate lessors or public databases; computationally analyzing or processing that information; and using that information to recommend rental prices, lease terms, or occupancy levels to a real estate lessor. Nonpublic competitor information is material lease information less than 365 days old that is not widely and readily available to the public at no cost. The coordination definition exempts owners of multiple properties for actions related exclusively to properties controlled by the same rental property owner. Licensed Real Estate Agents operating in accordance with all applicable state regulations are excluded from both the coordination and service-provider definitions.
rules.exemptions: The coordination definition exempts same-owner actions related exclusively to that owner's multiple properties. Compliant Licensed Real Estate Agents are excluded from the coordination and service-provider definitions. The residential dwelling unit definition excludes inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities.
